leg: LANE 4 — Sacramento (SMF) ending + whole-trip cash minimization (all remaining unbooked legs)
summary:
SMF VERDICT: No, you cannot end at SMF without adding cash — EXCEPT on one award vehicle and one leg. I priced 7 Europe/Asia→SFO vs →SMF pairs live on Google Flights: SMF carries a consistent +$182 to +$450 per person premium (avg ~$290/pp, ~$1,450 for 5). There is no nonstop SFO–SMF; every "hop" is a 2-3 segment backtrack via SEA/LAX/DEN. On awards: FLYING BLUE is the one program that gives SMF free (it prices origin-to-destination, so AMS→hub→SMF prices at the same 60k business / 25k economy floor as AMS→SFO). Virgin Atlantic does NOT (its Delta charts are nonstop-only; the domestic leg is a separate award). AerClub does NOT (Aer Lingus metal only, no partner awards). Alaska/Atmos DOES structurally (free connections to gateway) but is unfundable — Amex MR doesn't transfer to Atmos. The cheapest real answer: fly into SFO, where the family's car is already parked from their Oct 8 departure, and drive 90 min. Marginal ground cost $273 (off-airport parking $238 + fuel/toll $35) vs +$1,450 to buy SMF tickets. ONE EXCEPTION: leg (d), the team's SIN→home Oct 10, where SIN→SMF is $584 vs SIN→SFO $514 — only +$70/pp, which is cheaper than ground-transporting 3 people from SFO. Send the team to SMF, the family to SFO.

TWO BASELINES IN THE BRIEF ARE WRONG AND CHANGE THE ANSWER. (1) "Virgin Atlantic flat 50k/seat Delta One Europe-US" — Virgin's West Coast band is 67.5k standard / 77.5k peak, and Virgin raised ex-Europe surcharges to $1,000+/seat in both directions. For 5 that's 337-387k MR PLUS $5,000-5,500 cash — MORE CASH than just buying 5 economy tickets ($3,715). Virgin is dead for this trip. (2) "November is cheaper" — false for the ex-DBV cash floor. DBV→SFO is a flat $743 on Oct 25, 26, 27, 28, Nov 1 AND Nov 2 (Turkish via ZAG/IST). November helps award space, not cash fares. Bonus: I also resolved v4.1's open hard gate — EI61 DUB→SFO is live and bookable on Oct 25 ($725), Nov 1 ($685) and Nov 2 ($685). It operates on all your candidate dates.

RECOMMENDED ALLOCATION: spend 387,500 MR + 110,500 SkyMiles on exactly THREE legs and pay cash for the other five. Total remaining cash = ~$7,568, vs $36,821 if you bought the same cabins for cash, vs $10,284 if you flew bare economy everywhere and spent zero points. 137,882 MR left over.
1. Jarred SFO→ICN business (Sep 27) — 110,500 Delta SkyMiles, ~$6 cash. Use SKYMILES here, not MR. SkyMiles are your only illiquid currency and this is the sole leg where Delta prices acceptably; burning them here preserves all 525k MR. (Aeroplan 75-85k MR is the higher-cpp play at 5.26c/pt, but it consumes the flexible currency — hold it as the fallback if SkyMiles reprice.)
2. Jarred SIN→FCO business (Oct 10) — 75,000 MR → Qatar Privilege Club, Qsuites SIN-DOH-FCO, ~$270 cash. 1.47 c/pt.
3. Family+Jarred DBV→home (Oct 25 or Nov 1) — 312,500 MR → Aer Lingus AerClub, 62,500/seat off-peak DUB→SFO business ×5, ~$775 fees + $815 Ryanair FR3881 DBV→DUB = ~$1,590 cash. This is BOTH the lowest-cash option available ($1,590 beats even 5 economy tickets at $3,715) AND lie-flat. 7.65 c/pt against the $25,485 business cash fare.
Everything else is cash: team ×3 SFO→ICN $1,413 (OZ211 nonstop $471) · 4 pax ICN→SIN KE643 $704 · team ×3 SIN→SMF $1,752 · family ×4 SFO→FCO $1,440 (Condor $360) · 5 pax FCO→DBV Ryanair $120.

HONEST FRAMING YOU SHOULD SEE: against a same-cabin cash baseline the points save $29,253. Against a bare-economy-everywhere baseline they save only $2,716. Most of the "$29k saving" is a comfort upgrade you were never going to buy, not cash you were going to spend. If your objective is literally minimum dollars out the door and you'd fly economy, the points only move ~$2.7k. But since MR has no cash value and this is the trip it exists for, spending it still strictly reduces this trip's cash — so spend it, just in the order above.
caveats:
ALL fares are 1-passenger Google Flights searches scraped Aug 2 2026 from the server-rendered payload (script: /tmp/lane4/gf.py, raw results /tmp/lane4/r1.json-r4.json). Multi-passenger queries would not render, so 5-seat and 3-seat inventory at these fares is NOT confirmed — deep-discount buckets frequently hold only 1-4 seats and the party fare can be materially higher. Re-price every leg for the real party size before committing.

IRREVERSIBILITY: Amex MR transfers are one-way and permanent (confirmed in your own v3 research). Do NOT transfer 312,500 MR to AerClub before confirming 5 business saver seats are actually showing on the exact date on aerlingus.com's reward search. Same for the 75,000 to Qatar. A failed AerClub search after transfer strands 312k points in a program that only redeems on Aer Lingus metal — the worst outcome in this entire plan.

AERCLUB RISK IS THE LOAD-BEARING ASSUMPTION. Five business saver seats on a single EI61 is a large ask on a ~30-seat cabin. The 62,500 off-peak Zone 6 rate is corroborated but Avios took a devaluation on Dec 15 2025 — verify the live number. Fees: the $163.30/pp figure I found is for a US-origin (SFO→DUB); a DUB-origin will differ, so my $775 total for 5 is an estimate, not a quote. Aer Lingus also publishes a 2026 peak/off-peak calendar I could not retrieve — confirm Oct 25 / Nov 1 are off-peak before assuming 62.5k.

AEROPLAN DEVALUED JUNE 1 2026 and sources conflict on whether North America↔North Asia business survived at 75,000 or went to 85,000. Budget 85k if you use it as the leg-(b) fallback.

DELTA SKYMILES 110,500 for SMF→ICN Delta One is your own v6 live quote, not something I re-verified today. SkyMiles is fully dynamic; if it has repriced, fall back to Aeroplan.

FLYING BLUE 60k IS A FLOOR, NOT A PRICE — and it is the dynamic trap already flagged in your context: if fewer than 5 saver seats exist, it reprices the WHOLE party to flex (~142k each = 710k MR, over budget). This is why I ranked AerClub's published fixed chart ahead of it despite Flying Blue being the only free-SMF vehicle. The Aug promo (KLM premium economy AMS→SFO 30k, travel window through end of Jan 2027, book by Aug 31) is the safer Flying Blue play at 150k MR for 5 — but it is premium economy, not business, and it costs ~$910 MORE cash than AerClub.

QATAR added a seat-selection fee on business awards booked after Nov 3 2025 — ~US$100 per sector, non-refundable. SIN-DOH-FCO is two sectors, so add ~US$200 if Jarred wants to pick his suite. My $270 assumes he skips it.

RYANAIR FR3881 DBV→DUB at $163 and FR5975 FCO→DBV at $24 are base fares only. Five checked bags will add roughly $250-300 per sector on Ryanair — the FCO→DBV leg realistically lands at ~$400, not $120. Croatia Airlines OU385 at $203 includes bags and may be cheaper all-in for a 5-person party with luggage.

CONDOR SFO→FCO at $360 is an LCC-style fare via FRA; bags and seats are extra and the FRA connection is self-owned in irrops. TAP at $506 is the protected alternative.

The SFO parking figure ($8-27/day) comes from a single aggregator (Triply) — verify at flysfo.com. SFO is under Terminal 3 West construction through 2026; allow extra time.

I did NOT verify: live award space on any of the three recommended redemptions; whether the family actually has a car to park at SFO on Oct 8; Chase UR balance (your v7 notes it was never read — at ~34,700 it is too small to fund the 75k Aeroplan play the v7 audit proposed, which is a real error in that recommendation worth flagging).

If the true objective is minimizing cash outlay in absolute terms, points still win; if it is maximizing value per point, cash economy plus keeping the 525k MR intact is the stronger play.

caveats:
METHOD AND WHAT IS ACTUALLY VERIFIED. Fares come from a deterministic Google Flights TFS-protobuf scraper I built (working copy /tmp/lane1/gf.py; raw pulls in /tmp/lane1/matrix.json, p5.json, pos5.json, party.json, pos.json). It encodes trip-type, cabin, date and exact passenger mix into the URL rather than relying on natural-language parsing, and I validated it against known itineraries — returned flight numbers (EI603|EI61, AA741|AA2663, BA431|BA285, KL605) and prices decode cleanly from aria-labels. Positioning fares are cross-checked against the Ryanair farfnd v4 API, which is Ryanair's own booking engine and is authoritative. All figures pulled 2026-08-02 and are one-way economy; transatlantic cash moves daily and these will drift.

THE 4-SEAT CEILING IS THE FINDING TO ACT ON, AND IT NEEDS HUMAN CONFIRMATION. I established it by explicit pax-ladder testing rather than inference — every legacy DBV route prices smoothly at 1, 2, 3 and 4 passengers and then returns zero itineraries at 5, on every date tested (Oct 25, 26, 27, 28, Nov 1). Ryanair routes return 5 normally, which proves the query mechanism is not the constraint. The most likely mechanical explanation is that these carriers file a maximum of 4 seats in the cheapest bucket and Google will not split a party across buckets — meaning 5 may well be bookable at a higher fare, or as 4+1. What I have NOT verified is whether the 5th ticket actually prices near the first four. My 4+1 totals assume it does (I used the live 1-adult fare), and that assumption is the single largest source of error in this lane. Before committing to any of the top-8 options, call the carrier or an agent and confirm 5 seats on one PNR. Note also that the isolated-child query (0 adults + 1 child) returned inflated unaccompanied-minor pricing — I deliberately did not use those numbers.

COSTS I ADDED THAT THE RAW FARES HIDE. Transatlantic Basic economy carries no checked bag; BA and American publish $75 for the first transatlantic Basic bag under their joint-business alignment, so I added $375 for five bags to every option. Ryanair positioning fares exclude checked baggage entirely — five 20kg bags run roughly €250 (~$275), which I added to the Vienna, London, Dublin and Stansted paths and which is what pushes London from best-fare to ninth on total cost. I also added an Oct 25 gateway hotel night for five ($180-320 by city), because the Airbnb checks out Sunday Oct 25 and every transatlantic departure here is Oct 26 or later. These three lines total $700-950 and reorder the ranking materially; a fare-only comparison would mislead.

SEPARATE-TICKET RISK ON WINTER-TIMETABLE DAY ONE. Every option except the Dubrovnik through-ticket puts positioning and transatlantic on separate PNRs with no protection if the first leg slips. Oct 25 is day one of the winter timetable, historically the highest-churn schedule day of the year in Croatia, and several Dubrovnik routes are being cut at exactly this boundary. Ryanair is reportedly dropping Vienna and Brussels-Charleroi for winter 2026/27 while keeping Dublin and Krakow year-round — the Vienna flight still sells live in the API but may be among its last, so do not build on it without reconfirming. Frankfurt is the year-round nonstop and is the most schedule-robust positioning leg in the lane; the ~$250 premium over Barcelona is cheap insurance. Arriving the gateway the night before, which every option here already does, is the main mitigation.

FLIGHT NUMBERS ARE PARTIALLY UNRELIABLE; PRICES ARE NOT. Some decoded itinerary strings came back as artifacts (4H38, BB8, AL3) where the base64 payload did not yield clean carrier codes. Prices derive from aria-label attributes and are reliable; where I cite a specific routing (EI603|EI61, AA741|AA2663, BA681|BA285, FR3881, FR9756, OU663) the code decoded cleanly. Nonstop-versus-connecting labels come from a separate stop-count parse, which is how I confirmed LHR→SFO Oct 26 at $2,360 is genuinely nonstop.

TWO THINGS I DID NOT PRICE. First, ground transport SFO→Sacramento is estimated at $60-150 rather than quoted, since the family likely has a car or a pickup at home — it is small enough not to change any conclusion, and SMF loses by $1,800+ regardless. Second, the Nov 1-2 options require six additional nights of lodging somewhere in Europe which I costed only as a rough $1,400-2,100 range; that number deserves its own pass if the November extension is seriously considered, though the finding that November saves nothing on cash economy fares already undercuts the rationale.

Aer Lingus's reward search is login-gated (I hit it live and it returned no results without AerClub credentials), and Aeroplan/Flying Blue partner space for a party of five is the single biggest risk in every option here. Every points_cost below is a CHART PRICE, not a confirmed booking. Finding 5 economy award seats on one flight is realistic; finding 5 business seats is close to fantasy — LH releases ~2 J seats to partners until ~15 days out, and the Aer Lingus all-business line should be treated as aspirational. VERIFY SPACE BEFORE TRANSFERRING: Amex MR transfers are irreversible and confirmed so in your own v3 research. WHAT IS ESTIMATED: all taxes/surcharge figures are historical-typical from award blogs, not live quotes — AerClub economy ex-DUB ~£75 (~$100)/seat and business ~£250–300 (~$365)/seat are the load-bearing estimates behind the split-cabin math, and business YQ is the number most likely to be wrong. FLYING BLUE REMAINS THE TRAP your v7 audit identified: the 25,000 economy figure is a DYNAMIC FLOOR, and if fewer than 5 saver seats exist the whole party reprices to flex. I did confirm live that Air France serves DBV on Nov 1 (12:50 departure appeared in Google Flights), so a single FB ticket is structurally possible — but price it before you believe it. options.label: L3-F — SPLIT PROGRAM (3 Aeroplan + 2 AerClub): contingency, not a saving

Worked example: 3 pax on Aeroplan DBV→SFO (180,000 pts, ~$309 cash) + 2 pax on AerClub EI61 (32,500 Avios, ~$200 taxes + ~$505 positioning) = 212,500 points and ~$1,014. The REAL and only reason to split: award space. If Aeroplan releases 3 seats and AerClub 2, this is how you still get everyone home.

options.label: NON-UK DEPARTURE — quantified saving vs London
options.detail: Direct answer, with real numbers. UK Air Passenger Duty from 1 April 2026, Band B (2,001–5,500 mi, which covers LHR–SFO at 5,354 mi): £102 reduced rate (economy) and £244 standard rate (premium economy, business and first). Ireland ABOLISHED its air travel tax in 2014 and levies nothing, so departing Dublin instead of London saves the full APD: 5 economy seats = £510 ≈ $685 saved; 2 business + 3 economy = £794 ≈ $1,065 saved; 5 business = £1,220 ≈ $1,640 saved. Spain and Portugal are similar to Ireland in being low but not zero (Iberia ex-MAD runs ~$110–150/seat all-in). Germany levies a long-haul ticket tax but does NOT charge it to transfer passengers, so routing DBV→FRA→SFO on one ticket avoids it. VERDICT: Dublin is the single best gateway in Europe for this leg — no departure tax, US preclearance so you clear immigration before boarding and land at SFO domestically, AND the cheapest Avios chart of the whole family (16,250 vs BA's 90,000 for business on the identical aircraft). Never route the transatlantic DEPARTURE through the UK.
options.gateway: DUB strongly preferred; MAD acceptable; LHR to be avoided
options.getting_there: n/a
options.notes: One nuance: UK APD is charged on DEPARTURE from the UK, so a DBV→STN→DUB positioning routing pays only the trivial Band A rate (£15 economy) on the STN→DUB hop and never touches Band B. Transiting the UK is fine; DEPARTING the UK transatlantically is what costs.

options.label: THE 8-YEAR-OLD — child award discounts, definitive
options.detail: Direct answer: on the Avios programs there is NO child discount. British Airways, Iberia and Aer Lingus AerClub all charge children aged 2–11 the FULL adult Avios price and full taxes — only lap infants under 2 get the 10% rate, which is irrelevant here. So on every Aer Lingus option above, the 8-year-old costs exactly what an adult costs. Aeroplan likewise has no child discount. THE ONE EXCEPTION among your transfer partners is FLYING BLUE, which gives 25% off award tickets for children aged 2–11 travelling with an adult, in all cabins, on Air France and KLM metal only (not partners). Your 8-year-old qualifies; your 13- and 16-year-olds do not (both over 11). On a 25,000-mile economy award that saves 6,250 miles — real but small, roughly $50–90 of value, and not enough on its own to choose Flying Blue over Aeroplan or AerClub.
